descriptionChirho: A masculine noun denoting a helmet, a piece of military armor worn on the head for protection in battle. Appears exclusively in military contexts — equipping soldiers, describing warriors' armor, and in figurative descriptions of God's armor (Isa 59:17). All grammatical forms — singular construct (kova'), singular with conjunction (ve-kova'), plural with preposition (be-kova'im), plural with conjunction (ve-kova'im) — express the same concrete meaning. Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'helmet(s)', spa 'yelmo(s)/cascos' (helmet), hin 'top/topon' (टोप/टोपों, helmet), arb 'khuudhah/khuuadh' (خُوذَة/خُوَذِ, helmet), kor 'tugu(deul)' (투구/투구들, helmet), swa 'kofia za chuma' (iron cap/helmet).
